ios.desc:
Most iPad browsers treat it like a big iPhone. Beam treats it like the computer it is.

Built for researchers managing dozens of tabs, writers juggling multiple projects, developers who live in their browser, and anyone frustrated that Safari doesn't respect their iPad as a real computer.

"The closest I have ever gone to experiencing a desktop-like browsing experience on my tablet." - Digital Trends

"This is Arc, but for the iPad, and it's really good. I've actually been using this as my default browser." - Christopher Lawley

"Beam became my default immediately and made my iPad my primary laptop." - App Store review

Sidebar-first design
Instead of endless tab rows, Beam organizes everything into a persistent sidebar. Pinned tabs stay at the top. Today's tabs live in the middle. Projects and research go into spaces - separate workspaces you can switch between to keep contexts apart. Nest folders as deep as you need. Rename tabs, drag to reorder, collapse the sidebar when you want focus. Everything has its place.

Built for speed
A command bar gives you instant access to everything: open URLs, search history, switch tabs, trigger actions - all without lifting your hands from the keyboard. 56 keyboard shortcuts keep you in flow. Swipe gestures that actually make sense. Whether you're using a Magic Keyboard or just touch, Beam keeps you moving.

Beam Intelligence
Chat with your tabs using AI. Summarize pages, ask questions across multiple tabs, or get answers from what you're reading. Powered by on-device Apple Intelligence, or bring your own API key for cloud models.

Calmer web
Built-in ad blocking removes distractions by default. Multiple blocking levels let you choose how aggressive you want to be. The web feels quieter.

Actually designed for iPad
Beam follows modern iPadOS design - floating sidebar, smooth animations, layouts that work naturally with multitasking. Nothing is ported from Mac or scaled up from iPhone. It's built specifically for iPad, down to the last detail.

Beam is indie software, built by Henrik Singh in London - a browser that treats your iPad like the real computer it is.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Beam – A desktop-style browser for iPad built by a solo developer

quotes.text:
I’m a solo developer and I just launched Beam, a desktop-style browser for iPad.

Most iPad browsers still feel like stretched phone apps. Beam was built to feel closer to a real desktop productivity browser, with features like:

- Persistent sidebar with vertical tabs
- Spaces, favourites and pinned tabs
- Command bar and full keyboard shortcut support
- Memory-efficient tab lifecycle (active, warm, suspended tabs)
- Desktop-grade tab management designed specifically for iPad hardware limits

A big part of the work went into managing web views efficiently. iPads have much tighter memory constraints than desktops, so Beam unloads inactive tabs while keeping switching between active ones instant.

It’s a paid app ($4.99) with no subscriptions, no accounts, and no tracking beyond basic anonymised usage metrics.

App Store link:
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/beam-browser/id6756218494

I’d really appreciate any feedback, especially from people who use iPads heavily with keyboards.

Happy to answer questions.

More info: beambrowser.app
